Hi Amit / Emma —

Thanks for flagging this. Short version: Calendly/ChiliPiper sometimes shows the customer-local time correctly but the ICS it generates can default to UTC or a different TZ when the event falls in a DST cutover window. That mismatch is what likely created the 10:00 vs 02:00 confusion.

Two immediate options I can do right now:
- Send a manual .ics that explicitly pins Europe/London and Asia/Kolkata timezones (I can attach a two-invite approach so each attendee gets a calendar entry in their native zone).
- Create the event in our corporate Google Calendar with explicit TZ fields, then invite the guests (this tends to be the least ambiguous).

If you prefer self-serve fixes: have attendees open the Calendly link, confirm the timezone dropdown at the top (it sometimes reverts to the browser locale), and if the time falls on a DST transition day, pick a time at least 2 hours away from the transition.

I'll set up a manual invite and include an attached ICS that specifies both TZs and a short note about the DST cutover. Camila — can you double-check the timezone parameters if I hand this off? Jonas, can you confirm our canonical ICS template for cross-region invites?
